variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'his ten thousands' is plural, rendering the plural qere בְּרִבְבֹתָיו. The ketiv ברבבתו, lacking the plural yod, stands as a distinct reading only as the singular 'his ten thousand'; the ASV's plural does not render that.

coming in, paired with going out (rule 44).
מִן rendered since; the ASV writes the day separately, so no fusion.

The experiencer phrase בְּעֵינֵי the lords is recast as lords, following rule 6's nominal fusion. The noun carrying the written lexeme heads the unit; its independently rendered article remains separate.
Retained: the article takes the written the.

טוֹב supplies favor in the ASV's recast predication. The competing fusion with בְּעֵינֵי crosses independently rendered intervening material and fails rules 30 and 40's predicate-contiguity condition.
Retained: the explicit subject pronoun is recast as the object thee.
וְעַתָּה → Wherefore now: waw takes Wherefore, adverb takes now (rule 14).

עָשָׂה רַע בְּעֵינֵי rendered by the one verb displease; contiguous fixed expression fused under rule 30/40, headed on the verb; subject pronoun stays with it (rule 17). Competing reading: displease on the verb alone with the rest unrepresented.

The ASV recasts מִיּוֹם, from the day, as the duration expression so long, bounded by unto this day later in the clause. Neither so nor long has a clearly preferable independent allocation between מִן and יוֹם, so this residual phrase remains noncompositional under rules 2 and 6. The source head is יוֹם, carrying the temporal content, and the English anchor is long; rule 23 gives the content morpheme priority over the opening preposition, and rule 40 expressly extends the noun-headed temporal-adverb analysis to an absolute noun. Heading on מִן by the first-token fallback is the competing reading, but rule 6 requires the lexical-head rules to be considered before that fallback. The written אֲשֶׁר separately takes as, whose subordinating force is independently recoverable under rules 11 and 30; this corrects the chapter convention's whole-fusion premise.
The explicit temporal relative אֲשֶׁר takes as, linking the duration to I have been before thee; it is independently represented rather than fused with מִיּוֹם (rules 2, 11 and 30).
Modal and subject stay with the verb (rule 17).

Coordinator and subordinator written together at the clause edge for one waw: and as soon as is one rendering (rule 55), headed on the coordinator; competing head: soon.
